docs: Shared packages emit CommonJS. The API is a CommonJS NestJS app that requires them at runtime, and Node's ESM resolver demands explicit .js extensions on relative imports, which TypeScript does not add when emitting ESM from extensionless source.
Next.js bundles either format, so CommonJS costs the web app nothing.

composite is deliberately not set: it enables incremental build info that can leave a dist directory holding .d.ts.map files without the .d.ts files themselves after a partial clean, which fails consumers with an implicit-any error.
